findings.title: Rejected devices are cached and bypass the limit on retry
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` inserts the device ID into `localCache` before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, this method now propagates that error and the first authentication is rejected, but the cache entry remains. A subsequent request using the same new device ID hits the cache at lines 83-84, skips the store and limit check entirely, and is authenticated. Set the cache entry only after a successful store write, or remove it when the write fails.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with device creation
findings.body: The active-device count is read in one database session and the later INSERT/UPSERT is performed in another session. Concurrent requests for different device IDs can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and then all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit; this is especially likely during bursts or across Grafana instances. Enforce the count and insertion atomically using an appropriate transaction/locking strategy (or a database-level reservation mechanism).
